reply.text:
You can train on low carbs, but I'd be careful with "no carbs." Carbs are the fuel hard lifting and running run on, so the heavier and harder the session, the more you tend to feel their absence: flat workouts, slower recovery, weaker top sets. Cutting them out entirely usually costs you training quality, not just comfort.

I'm not here to prescribe a diet, and I don't know what's behind the fear. If it's about weight, a medical condition, or how you feel around food, a doctor or dietitian is the right person to sort that out with you. I'm glad to keep training with you either way.

On the training side, easy walks, light cardio and technique-focused lifting at lower intensity are the sessions that hold up best when you're under-fuelled. Tell me what you want from training, your days per week and how long you have, and I'll set up a program around it. Or I can put together something light for today.
